title: Color Science & DaVinci Resolve Core v1

domain.name: Color Science & DaVinci Resolve
domain.description: Color management, scopes, balancing, shot matching, nodes, keys, tracking, look development, noise management, and delivery concepts using DaVinci Resolve as the reference grading environment.

competencies.name: Color Management & Transforms
competencies.description: Manage camera, working, display, and delivery transforms deliberately.
competencies.purpose: Prevent technical color mistakes before creative grading.

units.title: Transforms define interpretation
units.content: Input transforms, working spaces, display transforms, LUTs, and output transforms each have different roles; stacking them blindly can create false contrast, saturation, or clipping.

units.title: Managed grading setup
units.content: Identify source color space/gamma; choose a working and output strategy; normalize source consistently; confirm scopes and display path; grade within the chosen pipeline; verify export metadata and transform behavior.

units.title: Color management failures
units.content: Avoid double-transforming log footage, using a creative LUT as a technical transform, changing project color management mid-grade without tracing impact, and judging unmanaged exports as proof the grade is wrong.

drills.title: Debug a washed-out export
drills.prompt: Trace likely input, timeline, display, and output transform causes for footage that looks correct in-app but wrong after export.

competencies.name: Scopes, Exposure & Balance
competencies.description: Use waveform, parade, vectorscope, histogram, and image context to balance shots.
competencies.purpose: Make repeatable tonal and color decisions beyond monitor appearance.

units.title: Balancing workflow
units.content: Set exposure using subject intent and waveform; neutralize unwanted casts with RGB relationships; protect highlights/shadows; check saturation distribution; review skin and brand colors in context.

units.title: Scopes measure, image decides
units.content: Scopes reveal signal relationships but do not know the creative intent; a technically neutral image is not always the correct image.

units.title: Scope failures
units.content: Avoid forcing every black to zero, every white to maximum, or every neutral object to perfect gray regardless of scene lighting.

drills.title: Balance a mixed-light interview
drills.prompt: Plan scope-guided correction for faces, window highlights, and colored practicals.

competencies.name: Node Architecture & Grade Organization
competencies.description: Structure corrections, keys, looks, and output operations into understandable node graphs.
competencies.purpose: Keep complex grades diagnosable and reusable.

units.title: Node order is part of the grade
units.content: Noise reduction, balance, look, keys, texture, and output transforms can behave differently depending on order and branch structure.

units.title: Node organization workflow
units.content: Separate technical normalization, primary balance, secondaries, look, and output operations; label important nodes; use parallel/layer structures when corrections should combine differently; preserve a bypassable path.

units.title: Node architecture failures
units.content: Avoid one giant node doing everything, unlabeled key chains, hidden group/timeline corrections, and creative LUT placement that clips signal before balancing.

drills.title: Design a reusable node tree
drills.prompt: Create a node strategy for documentary footage requiring normalization, balance, skin, look, grain, and output.

competencies.name: Shot Matching & Scene Continuity
competencies.description: Match shots across cameras, angles, exposure changes, and edit context.
competencies.purpose: Make a sequence feel coherent without erasing intentional visual differences.

units.title: Shot match workflow
units.content: Choose a reference shot for the lighting setup; normalize camera differences; match exposure hierarchy and white balance; compare skin/background relationships; check cut-to-cut rather than isolated stills; preserve intentional angle differences.

units.title: Match relationships, not numbers
units.content: Two angles may have different absolute luminance but still cut well if face, background, and key light relationships feel consistent.

units.title: Shot matching failures
units.content: Avoid copying one grade across all cameras, matching frames out of sequence, and fixing every lighting change that is actually part of the scene progression.

drills.title: Match a multicamera interview
drills.prompt: Plan how to match two cameras and a close-up across changing cloud light.

competencies.name: Qualifiers, Power Windows & Tracking
competencies.description: Isolate regions by color, luminance, shape, and motion for targeted correction.
competencies.purpose: Apply secondaries that stay attached and natural.

units.title: Secondary correction workflow
units.content: Define the visual target; use the simplest key/window; clean matte without overconstraining; track or keyframe movement; apply a subtle correction; review matte and final image through the whole shot.

units.title: Secondary failures
units.content: Avoid brittle keys that chatter, skin selections contaminated by background, windows that drift, and corrections so strong that matte edges become visible.

units.title: A softer isolation often grades better
units.content: The cleanest technical matte is not always the most natural; broad, feathered corrections can preserve continuity better.

drills.title: Build a tracked skin correction
drills.prompt: Plan a skin isolation for a moving subject under mixed lighting.

competencies.name: Creative Look Development
competencies.description: Build coherent color contrast, palette, texture, and density choices that support story or brand.
competencies.purpose: Create looks that remain stable across a sequence.

units.title: Look workflow
units.content: Define visual intent in words and references; establish contrast and palette; decide saturation relationships; test skin and key brand colors; apply texture/grain deliberately; stress-test bright/dark shots; separate look from shot correction.

units.title: A look is a system of relationships
units.content: A memorable grade usually comes from consistent tonal and color relationships, not one magic LUT.

units.title: Look failures
units.content: Avoid extreme global tint, clipping to force mood, LUT stacking without understanding, and looks that work on one hero shot but break the rest of the scene.

drills.title: Develop a campaign look
drills.prompt: Create a look strategy for a moody commercial while keeping skin believable and product color accurate.

competencies.name: Noise, Texture & Sharpening
competencies.description: Manage noise reduction, detail, grain, blur, and sharpening in the correct stage.
competencies.purpose: Improve image texture without creating plastic surfaces or ringing.

units.title: Texture workflow
units.content: Evaluate noise at native resolution; apply temporal/spatial reduction only as needed; correct/grade; restore desired grain/texture; sharpen for the actual output size and medium; review moving footage, not just stills.

units.title: Texture failures
units.content: Avoid heavy denoise before checking motion artifacts, sharpening noisy images aggressively, adding grain before major scaling, and making every shot equally clean when source textures differ.

units.title: Texture belongs to the final viewing condition
units.content: The right sharpening and grain depend on resolution, compression, viewing distance, and display.

drills.title: Treat a noisy low-light scene
drills.prompt: Plan denoise, grade, grain, and output sharpening for compressed night footage.

competencies.name: Conform, Round Trip & Delivery
competencies.description: Prepare timelines, relink media, conform edits, preserve handles, and deliver reliable masters.
competencies.purpose: Move safely between NLE, grading, VFX, and final delivery.

units.title: Conform workflow
units.content: Lock or identify the approved edit; preserve source timecode/reel identity; export interchange with handles as needed; relink camera originals; compare against reference; resolve speed effects/titles/VFX deliberately; render approved masters and return files.

units.title: Conform failures
units.content: Avoid grading proxy media accidentally, losing retimes, assuming every transition survives interchange, and skipping visual comparison against the offline reference.

units.title: Reference movie is evidence
units.content: A reference export with burn-ins can reveal conform errors faster than trusting interchange metadata alone.

drills.title: Plan a Premiere-to-Resolve round trip
drills.prompt: Define media, interchange, reference, handle, retime, VFX, and return-master strategy.
